findings.title: A registry read that fails for any reason lets a vector write through unchecked
findings.intended: ADR-0006 (refusable before it happens); FR-014 (enforcement is not opt-in).
findings.remedy: Raise from get_embedding_identity (and the inventory/quarantine reads) unless the registry is absent.
findings.notes: Pin code against a fake cursor raising SQLCODE -99 on the registry read: get_embedding_identity -> None and enforce_embedding_identity returns None (write proceeds). Not provoked live: revoking SELECT in AUDITA changes server security settings (forbidden). Reproduced live since steer 9 (rx-live-priv-vec): as the disposable least-privilege user, with a route cached and SELECT on the embedding registry revoked (CheckPrivilege 0), a vector write returned True and the row landed; earlier evidence used stand-ins.

observed.verdict: privilege error on the registry read turned the identity check off
observed.oracle: a registry read that fails for any reason but absence refuses the write

findings.title: Vectors from one model can be stored under another model's identity
findings.intended: ADR-0006: a vector's identity is the model that made it.
findings.remedy: Offer the identity of the model that produced the vector, or refuse cross-model fallback.
findings.notes: Live check blocked-access: IRIS EMBEDDING() configurations need %Embedding/AI Hub (P-0101), absent on Community 2026.1.
findings.observed: embed_text falls back to a Python embedder when the IRIS EMBEDDING() call fails (iris_vector_graph/_engine/embeddings.py:157-197); _encode_batch never calls IRIS EMBEDDING() (2033-2049); the offered identity comes from embedding_config first (iris_vector_graph/_engine/schema.py:1013-1018).

findings.title: The IRIS queue worker writes vectors with no identity check, and ignores the model for the default graph
findings.intended: ADR-0006 / spec 226: every seam that writes vectors consults the registry.
findings.remedy: Route default-graph entries through the registry and compare the entry's model and width before writing.
findings.notes: Live write path blocked-access: it needs a working EMBEDDING() config (absent on Community); without it the worker writes nothing at all (F-0604).
findings.observed: ProcessBatch targets Graph_KG.kg_NodeEmbeddings for every default-graph entry whatever its config (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/EmbedQueue.cls:280-286) and reads no registry row.

findings.title: The IRIS queue worker marks an entry DONE when no vector was made
findings.intended: SetResult: DONE carries the result vector, ERROR the message; VEC-I7.18.
findings.remedy: Set ERROR with the IRIS message on a failed Prepare, a negative SQLCODE or an empty result.

observed.verdict: entry DONE, no vector, no error
observed.oracle: an entry is DONE only with a stored vector; a failed EMBEDDING() is ERROR with the IRIS message

findings.title: enqueue_for_embedding checks the default table's row, not the target graph's route
findings.intended: Spec 227: kg_NodeEmbeddings' registry row is the default pair's row and nobody else's (embeddings.py:1992-1998).
findings.remedy: Resolve the target route (graph, config) and enforce against its row.
findings.observed: enqueue_for_embedding always enforces against ('kg_NodeEmbeddings', graph '') (iris_vector_graph/_engine/embeddings.py:1839-1842 at the pin's numbering: the enforce call before _ensure_queue_route).

findings.title: Erasure leaves IVF, tree and PLAID indexes holding an erased graph's ids and vectors
findings.intended: HD-0601 (assumption): retained vector-index contents are observable after erasure unless purged; graph-owned indexes must be invalidated or deleted. docs/migration/v4.0.0.md:742-750 names IVF a gap.
findings.remedy: Prune or invalidate graph-owned indexes in the erase; record the graph with the index.
findings.notes: After erase_graph removed the graph's 4 nodes, ivf_search answered the same 3 erased ids with the same scores and ivf_info still counts 4.

observed.oracle: HD-0601 (assumption): erasure leaves no graph-owned index answering the erased graph's ids

findings.title: The IVF index's 'cosine' metric is an unnormalised dot product
findings.intended: metric='cosine' is cosine similarity (VecIndex.Cosine normalises, VecIndex.cls:83-90).
findings.remedy: Normalise at build, insert and query time.
findings.notes: Query [1,1,0,0]: long45 [10,0,0,0] scored 10.0 above short0 [0.1,0.1,0,0] scored 0.2; cosine orders them the other way.

observed.oracle: cosine ranks short0 (cos 1.0) above long45 (cos 0.707), scores within [-1, 1]

findings.title: Vector index stores do not check width or duplicates
findings.intended: VEC-B11.14: an id lives in at most one cell; indexed counts distinct ids.
findings.remedy: Delete before insert across cells, count only new ids, refuse another width.
findings.notes: Re-inserting 'a' put it in cells 0 and 1, indexed 2 -> 3, and the stale vector still answered the old direction with score 1.0. VecIndex and PLAID branches of the finding were not run.

observed.oracle: an id lives in at most one cell; indexed counts distinct ids

findings.title: The fused search may read an IVF index built for another graph
findings.intended: FR-013 (a scoped lookup never widens); search_nodes_by_vector refuses the same case (vector.py:783-790).
findings.remedy: Refuse the IVF leg for an index of unknown or other graph; persist the graph with the index.
findings.observed: _fusion_leg_index falls back to an index whose graph is unknown, with a WARNING (iris_vector_graph/_engine/vector.py:208-225).

findings.title: The SQL kg_KNN_VEC answers no rows, without error, for a graph whose vectors are under a declared model
findings.intended: docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md:702-714 (such a call raises); 4.6.0 R265 (no silent empty answer).
findings.remedy: Have VectorRouteGuard refuse when the graph has any node route other than kg_NodeEmbeddings.
findings.notes: The engine's search_nodes_by_vector answers [('v1', 1.0)] for the same graph and model; SQL kg_KNN_VEC answers [].

observed.oracle: the SQL procedure answers the graph's vectors or raises; never an empty answer over held vectors

findings.title: Edge vectors the upgrade places in a named graph are not found by edge search, and the edge and text quarantines have no API
findings.intended: CONTEXT.md:159-161 (an operator places each quarantined vector); edge search resolves (graph, model, edge) routes.
findings.remedy: Route named-graph edge rows into kg_eemb_ tables or register kg_EdgeEmbeddings per graph; add list/place calls.
findings.notes: Live check needs a 3.2.0 fixture namespace (blocked-access: namespaces belong to the orchestrator).
findings.observed: The edge step inserts into kg_EdgeEmbeddings with the edge's graph_id (iris_vector_graph/migrations/statements.py:203-240) and adopts kg_EdgeEmbeddings for graph '' only (iris_vector_graph/_engine/schema.py:1312-1315).

findings.title: The edge and table searches skip rules the node search keeps
findings.intended: ADR-0005 forbids the lengthed TO_VECTOR form for a query vector; 4.6.0 R142 uses the route's dtype.
findings.remedy: Use the unlengthed form and the route's dtype; extend the routed-name refusal to kg_eemb_.
findings.observed: edge_vector_search builds TO_VECTOR(?, engine dtype, comma-counted dim) and answers [] for errors containing '-30', 'not found' or 'empty' (iris_vector_graph/_engine/vector.py:366-391).

findings.title: VectorOptimizer.migrate_to_optimized writes vectors without the identity check and reports success with failures
findings.intended: ADR-0006: every seam that writes vectors consults the registry.
findings.remedy: Enforce the identity, run as one transaction or report failure when failed > 0.
findings.observed: migrate_to_optimized inserts row by row with no enforce_embedding_identity and no transaction and returns success: True with a failed count (iris_vector_graph/vector_utils.py:151-280).

findings.title: embed_nodes and embed_edges count an identity refusal as an error and return normally
findings.intended: ADR-0006: spec 226 requires it to raise.
findings.remedy: Re-raise EmbeddingIdentityConflict.

observed.verdict: identity conflict counted as errors; returned normally

findings.title: A store_embeddings batch refused for a missing node can leave a new empty route behind
findings.intended: SYS-I3: a refused write changes no store (VEC-X3.9).
findings.remedy: Check every node before resolving the route.
findings.notes: Refused with 'Node does not exist', yet a 6-wide kg_emb_ route and its registry row exist afterwards.

observed.verdict: refused, yet a 6-wide route and registry row now exist
observed.oracle: a refused batch leaves the registry and routes as they were

values.call: refused ValueError: Node does not exist in graph 'barb230626': missing

findings.title: The embed selector's label filter crosses graphs, and its exclude pattern escapes without ESCAPE
findings.intended: Spec 227: selection is graph-scoped (embed_nodes docstring); an exclude pattern skips the matching ids (P-0603).
findings.remedy: Add the graph predicate to the label subqueries and ESCAPE '\' to the LIKE.
findings.notes: Two earlier runs failed in the harness's fake model (breadth-a-live-06-vectors, breadth-a-live-06-embed) but already showed the selection: total 3 nodes selected in g for label X with exclude x_*, where only xy1 qualifies.

observed.verdict: 'same' embedded via another graph's label; x_1 not excluded
observed.oracle: only g's nodes holding X in g are embedded; exclude x_* skips x_1

findings.title: The glossary and user guide say a second model's write is refused; the code routes it to its own table
findings.intended: CONTEXT.md:154-157 and docs/USER_GUIDE.md:958-960.
findings.remedy: Update CONTEXT.md and the USER_GUIDE.
findings.notes: p0610/p0614 probes in AUDITA created model-keyed routes without refusal, consistent with the code.
findings.observed: A write naming another model gets its own route (iris_vector_graph/_engine/embeddings.py:755-792); the upstream test test_same_width_different_model_gets_its_own_route asserts it.

findings.title: The ledger's node delete does not reach a default-graph node's routed vectors
findings.intended: The engine's delete_node (Eraser.EraseNodeIds) reaches every route; a ledger delete of the same node should too.
findings.remedy: Have LedgerApply.DeleteNodeRows delete from every node route the registry names for the default graph.

observed.verdict: ledger delete refused by the route's foreign key
observed.oracle: a ledger delete_node removes what the engine's delete_node removes (Eraser reaches every route)

findings.title: A node re-enqueued while a worker holds its old text is marked DONE with the old vector
findings.intended: enqueue_for_embedding docstring: re-enqueue overwrites, one entry per node (the latest request is the one to honour).
findings.remedy: Version each entry (a sequence stamped at enqueue) and set DONE only if the version is unchanged; or claim atomically.
findings.notes: New, from the model sub-lane (check vec_queue-as-built-reenqueue). HD-0604 assumes a single active consumer; even with one worker the enqueue/work interleaving loses the newer text.
findings.observed: ClaimPendingBatch is a plain scan with no claim state (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/EmbedQueue.cls:105-133); Enqueue overwrites a PENDING entry of the same graph (EmbedQueue.cls:44-58); the worker then sets DONE for the entry id with the vector of the text it read before.

findings.title: kg_KNN_VEC's route guard picks an arbitrary registry row where Python applies a fixed preference
findings.intended: Route resolution is one rule across surfaces (embeddings.py:107-118 orders the candidates).
findings.remedy: Apply the Python preference in the guard (ORDER BY it) or refuse when more than one row qualifies.
findings.notes: New, from the storage-order disposition; reachability (two unkeyed node rows for one graph) not shown.
findings.observed: VectorRouteGuard selects TOP 1 table_name over registry rows keyed (table_name, graph_id), so two node rows for one graph with no model key answer in scan order (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/GraphStores.cls:300-312).

findings.title: The 4.0.0 vector migration takes an undeclared legacy table's width from an arbitrary row
findings.intended: Migration sizes a route from the data it moves; rows of several widths are a quarantine case.
findings.remedy: Measure every distinct width and refuse/quarantine a mixed table.
findings.notes: New, from the storage-order disposition; a 3.x fixture with mixed widths would be needed to provoke it.
findings.observed: _Migrator._measured_width reads one stored vector with no ORDER BY when neither the table nor the registry declares a width (iris_vector_graph/migrations/graph_scoped_embeddings.py:1265-1280).

findings.title: The embed queue serves PENDING entries in node-id order, so an entry can wait indefinitely
findings.intended: A queue that is worked repeatedly eventually serves every entry (progress; HD-0604 single consumer).
findings.remedy: Serve in arrival order (a sequence subscript) or round-robin from the last reqId.
findings.notes: New, from the storage-order disposition (collation-ordered, not storage-ordered). A progress (AG EF) model with an unbounded arrival stream would show it; the bounded vec_queue model drains because arrivals are bounded.
findings.observed: ClaimPendingBatch and ProcessBatch take the first batchSize PENDING entries in reqId (= node id) collation order (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/EmbedQueue.cls:112-133, 258-268); under steady enqueueing of low-collating ids a high id is never reached.

findings.title: SQL kg_KNN_VEC answers a node once per label, so a multi-label node takes several of the k places
findings.intended: kg_KNN_VEC is a k-nearest-nodes search over the default route (schema.py:2437-2483); kg_RRF_FUSE's vector leg calls it with no label filter (schema.py:2558).
findings.remedy: Use EXISTS for the label filter (no join when no filter is given), or SELECT DISTINCT node_id.
findings.notes: New, from the storage-order sub-lane's note; reproduced: a node with labels LA and LB filled both places of k=2 and pushed out the second-nearest node.

observed.oracle: k nearest nodes: each node at most once; with k=2 both a and b answer
